title: Power Automate: schedule desktop flows directly with scheduled triggers
summary: The roadmap description, licensing and metering statements, and data policy controls are supported. Independent searches found no documentation resolving the narrowly stated scheduled-trigger gaps. The cloud-flow ownership statement needs an additional source citation.

claims.claim: Makers can run desktop flows on a recurring schedule directly from the Power Automate automation center.
claims.quote: Scheduled triggers enable makers to run desktop flows on a recurring schedule directly from the Power Automate automation center

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the scheduled-trigger capability's default state on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate schedule desktop flows directly automation center licensing default prerequisites identity connection data policy queue. Read roadmap, automation center overview and trigger prerequisites; no scheduled-trigger default found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Mixed describes the documented desktop-flow licensing routes: user licensing, unattended capacity and pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Power Automate supports both user and capacity licensing. ... For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licensing requirement specific to scheduled triggers is published.

Read licensing types, meters and cloud-trigger prerequisites; no separate requirement found.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant or environment UI setting or API to enable or disable scheduled triggers specifically is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" "desktop" "tenant"; "scheduled triggers" "desktop" "entity"; Power Automate desktop scheduled triggers disable tenant setting Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin Dataverse schedule entity. Read automation center and machines; no specific switch found.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center route through Security, Settings, Data and privacy, Data policy, policy, Edit Policy and Prebuilt connectors reaches connector classification using Move to Business.
claims.quote: In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... select a policy, and then select Edit Policy. ... Select the Prebuilt connectors step in the Edit Policy process. ... select Move to Business from the top menu bar.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <classification> classifies connectors and desktop flow modules in the named policy.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]> ... providers/Microsoft.ProcessSimple/operationGroups/DesktopFlow.Scripting (for Desktop Flow modules)

claims.claim: Showing desktop flow action groups in the data policy UI requires enabling Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies first.
claims.quote: By default, desktop flow action groups don't appear when you're creating a DLP policy. You need to turn on the Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies setting in your tenant settings.

claims.claim: Desktop flow modules must be explicitly classified for DLP evaluation to enforce their classification.
claims.quote: However, only desktop flow modules that are explicitly classified in a policy group (Business, Non-business, or Blocked) are enforced during DLP evaluation.

claims.claim: Classification values General, Confidential and Blocked correspond to Non-business, Business and Blocked respectively.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.quote: A registered machine or machine group that will run the triggered desktop flows.

claims.claim: The cloud-flow triggering route requires a work or school account.
claims.quote: A work or school account.

claims.claim: The cloud flow's owner is part of how a scheduled cloud flow is governed.
claims.quote: If the flow is a scheduled or automated flow, after the owner changes, the flow runs under the license of the new owner and uses their Power Platform request limits.
claims.fix: Add 'Change the owner of a cloud flow' (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/change-cloud-flow-owner) to sources for the ownership premise in Why it matters.

claims.claim: Data policy checks govern the documented cloud-flow route to a desktop flow.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe this automation-center scheduled-trigger feature's behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" "desktop flows". Read automation center overview, Manage machines and Trigger desktop flows from cloud flows; results describe cloud triggering, Windows Task Scheduler and Automation Kit, not the new feature.

claims.claim: No source found says the feature changes existing flows or schedules on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate schedule desktop flows directly automation center licensing default prerequisites identity connection data policy queue. Read roadmap, automation center and cloud-trigger documentation; no migration or change to existing schedules stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap does not identify the scheduled run's identity or connection.
claims.quote: Users can configure daily, weekly, monthly, hourly, or custom recurrence patterns, select the execution machine or machine group, and monitor upcoming scheduled runs from a centralized experience.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not specify what data a scheduled run can reach beyond the desktop flow itself.
claims.quote: Scheduled Triggers simplify desktop automation management and provide a more intuitive scheduling experience for attended and unattended desktop flows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies classify desktop flow modules as Business, Non-business or Blocked.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: Noncompliant desktop flows are suspended when evaluated against desktop-module data policies.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: A difference between scheduled-trigger and cloud-triggered DLP evaluation is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate schedule desktop flows directly automation center licensing default prerequisites identity connection data policy queue. Read DLP policy creation and automation center overview; neither describes a scheduled-trigger-specific evaluation difference.

claims.claim: The unattended-run page says unattended desktop flows require an available machine with all users signed out.
claims.quote: Unattended desktop flows require an available machine with all users signed out.

claims.claim: The unattended-run page warns that locked Windows user sessions prevent unattended runs.
claims.quote: Locked Windows user sessions will prevent unattended desktop flows from running.

claims.claim: Unattended mode executes desktop flows without human supervision.
claims.quote: Unattended run mode refers to a desktop flow execution without human supervision

claims.claim: The queue page says a timeout occurs if a desktop flow does not run within 12 hours after being requested.
claims.quote: A time-out occurs when desktop flows don't run within 12 hours after being requested.

claims.claim: The queue page says its orchestration rules apply to desktop flow runs scheduled by any user on the same device.
claims.quote: The presented orchestration rules apply to desktop flow runs scheduled by any user on the same device.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe the replacement troubleshooting experience for direct scheduled triggers.
claims.quote: Searched: "scheduled triggers" "desktop flows". Read automation center overview, Manage machines and Trigger desktop flows from cloud flows; only general monitoring and cloud-trigger troubleshooting described, not direct scheduled-trigger troubleshooting.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A data policy can manage both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.
claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors. ... The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether direct schedules use the desktop flow connector.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate schedule desktop flows directly automation center licensing default prerequisites identity connection data policy queue. Read DLP policy creation, automation center and cloud-trigger pages; none identifies the connector used by direct scheduled triggers.

claims.claim: The documented tenant-level data policy steps require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policy steps require Environment Admin permissions, or System Administrator for environments with Dataverse.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Variable cost is supported by desktop-flow per-run metering, so additional recurring runs can increase charges.
claims.quote: The Power Automate meters enable users to build and/or run premium Power Automate flows and to pay for their usage based on the number of times these flows run instead of purchasing standalone Power Automate licenses.

claims.claim: The roadmap item names no licence or meter.
